tools.name: steady_get_publication
tools.description: Get the publication the API key belongs to: title, Steady page URL, member counts (paying, trial, free, guest, external), monthly income and whether it is public. Good first call. Steady API: GET /publication.

tools.name: steady_list_plans
tools.description: List the publication's membership plans with state (draft, published, archived), currency, monthly and annual amounts, benefits and whether the plan is hidden. Steady API: GET /plans.

tools.name: steady_list_subscriptions
tools.description: List the current subscriptions (in_trial, active, not_renewing, guest, external and their terminated states): state, period (monthly or annual), amounts, currency, expiry and the subscriber and plan. Contains personal data. Steady API: GET /subscriptions.

tools.name: steady_list_inactive_subscriptions
tools.description: List the ended subscriptions (cancelled and expired, with cancelled-at and expires-at) with the subscriber and plan. Contains personal data. Steady API: GET /subscriptions/inactive.

tools.name: steady_list_newsletter_subscribers
tools.description: List the newsletter subscribers (email and the time they confirmed the opt-in). Contains personal data. Steady API: GET /newsletter_subscribers.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: steady_get_publication, steady_list_newsletter_subscribers · Private data: steady_get_publication · Public sink: steady_list_newsletter_subscribers.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: steady_get_publication, steady_list_newsletter_subscribers · Private data: steady_get_publication · Public sink: steady_list_newsletter_subscribers

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
